name: Dil Khushal (Besan Chakki)
instructions: 1. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and add besan, roasting it on low heat until it turns aromatic and golden brown.
2. Add the milk to the roasting besan to create a grainy texture, stirring continuously until the milk evaporates.
3. In a separate pan, prepare a one-string consistency sugar syrup by boiling sugar and water.
4. Pour the sugar syrup into the roasted besan mixture, adding cardamom powder, and stir until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
5. Grease a tray with ghee and transfer the mixture, spreading it evenly to a thickness of about an inch.
6. Garnish with chopped nuts and silver varq, allow it to cool completely, then cut into diamond or square shapes.
description: Dil Khushal, also known as Besan Chakki, is a classic Rajasthani dessert often prepared during festivals and weddings. The name 'Dil Khushal' translates to 'happiness of the heart,' reflecting its rich, indulgent taste and its role as a beloved celebratory sweet in Marwari cuisine.
